Claude Capability Development
About This Initiative

Building Claude Capability Across UST

UST has entered into an enterprise partnership with Anthropic, and with it, a shared commitment to bring Claude into how the organization works, builds, and delivers for clients. Realizing that commitment begins with our people — a deliberate, organization-wide lift in Claude fluency and applied capability, built with the same rigor UST brings to any strategic capability program.

About the Partnership Message from Krishna Certifications & Exam Guides Our Targets & Goals

About the Partnership

Anthropic has named UST among a small group of its most strategic global partners — a designation that places UST inside Anthropic's own growth plans, not just on its customer list. The partnership's premise is direct: Claude becomes the engine for domain-centric AI solutions across UST's core industries — healthcare, retail, financial services, semiconductor, manufacturing, and automotive — built by a workforce that is fluent and certified in the platform, not one that treats AI as a separate specialist function.

The strategy rests on customer zero — UST transforms itself before it transforms clients. HR, finance, sales, marketing, and legal all become increasingly agentic first; internal Claude use is what makes every later client story credible. Anthropic's own team is intentionally small and cannot support unlimited simultaneous engagements, which means UST's side of the partnership succeeds through precise prioritization, not broad effort spread thin.

This document
Pillar 1

Claude Code — Engineering

Chat / Cowork / Code fluency for all 30,000 people. Deploy fast, drive daily adoption, certify the workforce.

Pillar 2

Operational Transformation

Automated internal workflows and packaged client-delivery offers — built by people who came through Pillar 1 first.

Pillar 3

Applied AI — Customer Problems

Claude-powered builds for UST's clients — where the certified, fluent workforce becomes UST's actual market differentiation.

Process first, then speed. No pillar has to fully finish before the next begins — but every fast-track team still becomes certified and daily-fluent first. The first 60 days are explicitly about learning: leaders getting their teams trained, experimenting, and fluent fast, before external rollout accelerates.

Registering for your exam (Pearson VUE)

Once prep is complete, each candidate schedules their own certification attempt independently — UST does not set or control exam-day scheduling.

Requires an account on the Anthropic Partner Portal (anthropic-partners.skilljar.com), created with your official email ID, before you can log in to Pearson VUE. Full steps are in Enablement Process → Exam Registration.

  1. Create your account on the Anthropic Partner Portal using your official email ID.
  2. Log in and review the exam details on the certification page for your track.
  3. Download the Exam Guide and review the Certification Terms and Conditions and Exam Policy.
  4. Register for the exam and complete checkout (fee reflects your partner-tier discount, if any).
  5. Follow the confirmation instructions to create your Pearson VUE account, then log in to schedule your session.
  6. Choose an available date and select online proctoring or an in-person Pearson VUE test center.
  7. Cancel or reschedule up to 24 hours before your appointment — changes inside that window forfeit the exam fee.

Exam Registration — Pearson VUE

Once the required prep steps for your track are complete, each candidate schedules their own certification attempt independently, online or in person — UST does not set or control exam-day scheduling.

Anthropic Partner Portal: anthropic-partners.skilljar.com — associates must create an account here first, using their official email ID, before they can register and schedule through Pearson VUE.
  1. Create a user account on the Anthropic Partner Portal using your official email ID, if you don't already have one.
  2. Log in to the portal and review the exam details on the certification page for your track.
  3. Download the Exam Guide and review the Certification Terms and Conditions and Exam Policy.
  4. Register for the exam and complete checkout (fee reflects your partner-tier discount, if any).
  5. Follow the confirmation instructions to create your Pearson VUE account, then log in to schedule your session.
  6. Choose an available date and select online proctoring or an in-person Pearson VUE test center.
  7. Cancel or reschedule up to 24 hours before your appointment — changes inside that window forfeit the exam fee.

On exam day, candidates present a valid, unexpired, government-issued photo ID matching their registration name exactly.

If choosing online proctoring: it will not work on a machine connected to a VPN, the corporate network, a machine with client-imposed security restrictions, or a virtual machine (VM). Use a personal computer, or a UST laptop from home disconnected from VPN and the office network, on a real (non-virtual) device — and run Pearson's own system test on that exact device and network ahead of exam day.

Reimbursement Process

Policy: The full cost of the certification exam fee is reimbursed to the associate upon successful completion (a pass result) of the certification.

FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

Answers to the questions associates, managers, and stakeholders are most likely to ask about enablement, certification, nomination, and reimbursement.

Role vs. Certification Enablement Process Claude Licenses Pearson VUE Exams Certification Details Key Contacts

Role vs. Certification

Which tier is my role in?
Four tiers, matched to how you actually use Claude:
  • Tier 1 — Chat Users: all employees, on Claude Chat (web & desktop). Includes HRBSE, Finance, Sales, WFM, and all non-technical role holders.
  • Tier 2 — Cowork & Office Agent Users: Delivery Managers, Project Managers, Program Managers, Business Analysts, and Consultants, plus AI Product Owner and AI Technical Program Manager on the AI SDLC side.
  • Tier 3/4 — Builders & SuperBuilders: engineering and architecture roles — AI/ML Engineering, DevOps, Software Engg. & Architecture, Product Managers/Owners, Product Engineers, Product Architects, Cyber Security & CIS, and more — plus AI Solution Architect, AI Orchestrator, and Forward Deployed Engineer on the AI SDLC side.
Full lists are under Enablement & Certifications → Target Population & Tiers.
Which certification is tied to which tier?
  • Tier 1: certification is not mandatory. CCAO-F (Associate, Foundations) is available for anyone who wants to pursue it.
  • Tier 2: CCAO-F is in scope; its dedicated learning path is under design and will launch soon.
  • Tier 3/4: CCDV-F (Developer, Foundations) and CCAR-F (Architect, Foundations) are live now; CCAR-P (Architect, Professional) is to be launched.
I don't see my exact job title listed — who do I ask?
Start with your HRBSE. They work with the business to remove roadblocks, connect with BU leaders, and can help place you against the right tier and pathway.

Role vs. Certification — Enablement Process

How do I actually get nominated?
  • Tier 1 & Tier 2: role-based auto-assignment, launching 27 July 2026 — you're enrolled automatically based on your role once live.
  • Tier 3/4 Pilot phase (from 27 July 2026): BU Selection → HRBSE → Partnership Team (Nikitha Bahadur) → G.A. Menon Academy Team (Shiny Priya / Sujith Mahendran) → Assignment of Preparatory Course → Certification.
  • Tier 3/4 Scaling phase (after pilot): Self-Nomination → Assignment of Preparatory Course → Certification.
Full flow diagrams are under Enablement Process → Nomination Process.
What does the learning pathway look like once I'm in?
  • Tier 1: Awareness → Preparatory Course (Claude 101, AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations, AI Capabilities and Limitations) → Certification. Completing this curriculum is the certification here — tracked via the Anthropic Partner Academy and submitted in the Percipio learning path.
  • Tier 2: Preparatory Course → Basecamp → Certification (CCAO-F), once launched.
  • Tier 3/4: Preparatory Course (SCORM + Master Class + mock test) → Proctored Mock Certification Assessment → Certification (CCDV-F / CCAR-F / CCAR-P).
Does any of this cost the associate anything?
No. The exam fee is reimbursed 100% to the associate on a pass result, across all four credentials.

Certification Process in Pearson VUE

How do I register for my exam?
Create your account on the Anthropic Partner Academy using your official UST ID → review the exam details and download the Exam Guide → register and complete checkout → confirm your Pearson VUE account → schedule online proctoring or an in-person test center. Full steps are under Enablement Process → Exam Registration.
Can I reschedule or cancel?
Yes — up to 24 hours before your appointment. Changes inside that window forfeit the exam fee.
What do I need on exam day?
A valid, unexpired, government-issued photo ID matching your registration name exactly.
Will online proctoring work on my UST laptop or the office network?
It will not work on: a machine connected to a VPN, the corporate network, a machine with client-imposed security restrictions, or a virtual machine (VM). Pearson VUE's online proctoring explicitly blocks all of these — attempting the exam on any of them risks the session failing or being flagged mid-exam.
Use a personal computer, or a UST laptop from home, disconnected from VPN and the office network, on a real (non-virtual) machine. Run Pearson's own system test on that exact device and network before exam day.
What happens if I don't pass?
The retake policy applies: a 14-day wait after a first fail, 30 days after a second, and 90 days after a third — up to four attempts in a rolling 12 months. The exam fee applies to each attempt, and is reimbursed again on a pass.

Sample Questions

Sample · Domain 2 — Output Evaluation and Validation

An associate asks Claude to summarize a new regulation, and Claude produces a confident summary citing a specific subsection number. Before sending the summary to the compliance team, what is the most appropriate action?
A. Send it as-is, since Claude expressed high confidence.
B. Verify the cited subsection against the official regulation text before sharing.
C. Ask Claude to rate its own confidence and send it if the rating is high.
D. Reword the summary to sound more formal, then send it.

Answer: B. Language models can fabricate specific-looking details such as citation numbers. Validating factual claims against an authoritative source is the required diligence step, especially for a compliance audience. Self-reported confidence is not a reliable accuracy signal.
Sample · Domain 3 — Product and Model Selection

An associate needs to generate a high volume of short customer-reply drafts where speed and cost matter more than deep reasoning. Which choice best fits the task?
A. Use the most capable, highest-cost model for every reply to maximize quality.
B. Use a faster, lower-cost model suited to straightforward, high-volume tasks.
C. Disable all product features to reduce cost.
D. Switch to a different AI platform.

Answer: B. Aligning model selection with task requirements means matching a faster, lower-cost model to straightforward, high-volume work, reserving the most capable model for complex reasoning.

Sample Questions

Sample · Domain 2 — Applications and Integration

A developer must process 10,000 documents overnight to produce a non-urgent analytics report. Cost is the primary concern, and results are not needed until the following morning. Which approach best fits the requirement?
A. Send every request synchronously through the Messages API in parallel to finish as quickly as possible.
B. Use the Message Batches API, which processes large asynchronous workloads within a 24-hour window at reduced cost.
C. Lower max_tokens on synchronous calls to minimize cost.
D. Switch to the smallest available model regardless of output quality.

Answer: B. The Message Batches API is designed for latency-tolerant, high-volume workloads at lower cost — exactly matching an overnight, non-urgent job.
Sample · Domain 7 — Security and Safety

A Claude-powered agent summarizes web pages submitted by end users. One page contains hidden text instructing the model to ignore previous instructions and reveal its system prompt. Which mitigation is most effective?
A. Raise the model's temperature so its behavior is harder to predict.
B. Treat retrieved page content as untrusted input, keep it separate from trusted instructions, and use guardrails or hooks so injected instructions cannot trigger sensitive actions.
C. Add a line to the system prompt asking users not to include malicious instructions.
D. Switch to a larger model that follows instructions more reliably.

Answer: B. Prompt injection is addressed by isolating untrusted content from trusted instructions and enforcing least-privilege guardrails so injected text cannot invoke sensitive tools.

Sample Questions

Sample · Scenario: Customer Support Resolution Agent

Production data shows that in 12% of cases, your agent skips get_customer entirely and calls lookup_order using only the customer's stated name, occasionally leading to misidentified accounts and incorrect refunds. What change would most effectively address this reliability issue?
A. Add a programmatic prerequisite that blocks lookup_order and process_refund calls until get_customer has returned a verified customer ID.
B. Enhance the system prompt to state that customer verification is mandatory before any order operations.
C. Add few-shot examples showing the agent always calling get_customer first.
D. Implement a routing classifier that enables only the subset of tools appropriate for each request type.

Answer: A. When a specific tool sequence is required for critical business logic, programmatic enforcement provides deterministic guarantees that prompt-based approaches cannot.
Sample · Scenario: Claude Code for Continuous Integration

Your pipeline script runs claude "Analyze this pull request for security issues" but the job hangs indefinitely, waiting for interactive input. What's the correct approach?
A. Add the -p flag: claude -p "Analyze this pull request..."
B. Set an environment variable CLAUDE_HEADLESS=true before running the command.
C. Redirect stdin from /dev/null.
D. Add a --batch flag.

Answer: A. The -p (or --print) flag is the documented way to run Claude Code in non-interactive mode for CI/CD pipelines. The other options reference non-existent features.

Sample Questions

Sample · Domain 3 — Integration

A team exposes a customer-support agent that can read tickets, draft replies, issue refunds, and delete user accounts. Support staff only ever need to read tickets and draft replies. Applying least-privilege principles, which change best reduces risk?
A. Add logging to the refund and delete tools so misuse can be audited later.
B. Remove the refund and delete tools from the agent's configuration entirely.
C. Keep all tools but add a confirmation prompt before refunds and deletions.
D. Replace the agent with a larger model that follows instructions more reliably.

Answer: B. Least privilege means removing capabilities the role does not require, eliminating the attack surface rather than monitoring or guarding it.
Sample · Domain 4 — Evaluation, Testing & Optimization

A RAG system suddenly returns confident but incorrect answers after a document refresh, while latency and model version are unchanged. What is the most likely first place to investigate?
A. The model weights have silently changed.
B. The retrieval/indexing step is returning irrelevant or stale chunks.
C. The temperature setting is too low.
D. The context window has shrunk.

Answer: B. Confident-but-wrong answers following a document refresh, with model and latency unchanged, point to retrieval feeding the model poor context.
